messages:
customer:PixelPlay: Hey, running into a weird thing with streaming responses. App shows partial output, then the client reconnects and we get duplicated last chunk + a scramble. Mostly on iOS when switching from office WiFi to cellular. Happened ~15:12 PST.

alex (support): Sorry about that — can you paste a short repro (headers + client logs) and the request id if available? Is this SSE or websockets?

customer:PixelPlay: It's SSE (EventSource). Headers look normal. We use a small chunking wrapper so each chunk has a `chunk_id`. I'll paste client log snippets. No request id in app logs yet — can forward a server trace if you need.

customer:PixelPlay: ```
[15:12:02] EventSource connected -> /v1/streams/generate
[15:12:08] partial chunk received: chunk_id=abc123 text="The quick brown"
[15:12:09] network: interface changed WiFi->Cellular
[15:12:09] EventSource closed (code=0)
[15:12:10] reconnecting in 2s
[15:12:12] new EventSource connected -> same URL
[15:12:13] got chunk chunk_id=abc123 text="The quick brown" (again)
[15:12:13] got chunk chunk_id=def456 text=" fox jumps over"
[15:12:13] final assembly ended up duplicating middle text
```

alex (support): Thanks. From that it looks like the client reconnected and server re-sent the last in-progress chunk. Repro on Android/iOS? Any custom retries?

customer:PixelPlay: iOS only so far. We do automatic reconnect with exponential backoff. We don't pass Last-Event-ID. Our wrapper expects idempotency keys (chunk_id) so we can dedupe on client, but the UI concatenation logic doesn't check dedupe robustly.

alex (support): Two angles: 1) client dedupe (recommended), 2) server-side avoidance of duplicate replay for in-flight partials. I'm going to pull in eng-oncall to see whether streaming back-pressure/fallbacks could cause resends. @sara can you take a look?

sara (eng-oncall): looking. Can you attach the server trace/context id? Without that we can only guess. Related questions: was any model fallback triggered (we've seen fallback variants resend prefix tokens on reconnect), and was the request proxied through an intermediate load balancer that might have retried?

customer:PixelPlay: I don't have trace id in the app, but I can run the request from curl to get the server X-Request-Id. Example curl we used: ```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -N "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/generate" -d '{"prompt":"story","stream":true}'
```
I'll reproduce and paste headers.

tom (ios): quick note — iOS networking sometimes reuses connections when switching network stacks which can lead to the TCP reset and immediate reconnect. EventSource lib will happily re-subscribe. If server doesn't support resume semantics, you'll get repeated partials. We saw this with ALB health-checks earlier.

nina (android): Android usually closes and opens cleanly; less flaky here.

reconnect-bot: Incident check: no active platform-wide streaming incidents in last 24h.

sara (eng-oncall): If you can get the X-Request-Id from a reproducer that'd help. Meanwhile from runtime side: possible causes — (A) proxy retry replaying request to backend (B) server fallback to compatible model variant that replays prefix on reconnect (C) KV/prefix cache returning a cached prefix chunk when reconnecting due to different connection context. We'll look at logs for request around 15:12.

alex (support): Action items for PixelPlay: 1) quick client mitigation: dedupe incoming chunks by `chunk_id` before appending (defensive). 2) if you can, send Last-Event-ID header or include your `chunk_id` in EventSource `Last-Event-ID` field on reconnect so server can drop already-ack'd chunks. 3) reproduce with curl/pod from same network transition and paste server X-Request-Id.

customer:PixelPlay: Implemented client dedupe as a quick patch, we'll test. Running a curl repro now and will paste the X-Request-Id.

sara (eng-oncall): On our side I pulled the runtime logs for that 15:12 window (using a provisional trace id the customer gave in DM). Observed: front-proxy logged a downstream connection reset (RST) at 15:12:09, backend received a new connection at 15:12:12 with a different connection id. No explicit 5xx from backend. I do see `resume_hint: none` in our stream control logs for that session, which means the runtime didn't have an authoritative resume token for mid-stream replay. But I do see `sent_chunk(chunk_id=abc123)` twice — first on initial connection and then again when a fallback policy routed to a different serving pool about 3s later. That suggests the request was re-routed (smart routing) and the new pool replayed the last in-progress chunk.

alex (support): So likely interplay of network switch -> front-proxy reconnect -> smart routing fallback -> resend of last chunk.

sara (eng-oncall): Correct. Short-term recommendation: client dedupe + include Last-Event-ID. Medium-term: we'll add server-side guard to avoid re-emitting identical in-flight chunk_ids when resume_hint is none and the request appears to be a reconnect within a short window. I'll open an eng-runtime ticket.

alex (support): Filed ENG-STREAM-1427 to add de-dup guard and to log the `chunk_id` replay paths. Assigned to eng-runtime.

customer:PixelPlay: Great, thanks. We'll roll out the client dedupe patch to iOS and see if it mitigates. Will follow up with the X-Request-Id when repro'd via curl.

tom (ios): FYI for mobile app teams: make your client avoid optimistic append until you see at least one more token or a small debounce (100-200ms) to reduce visual duplication on reconnects.

sara (eng-oncall): noted. I'll keep the ticket open and update after a runtime change. If you can get a curl repro id that will speed up the root-cause.

alex (support): Marking as in-progress. If PixelPlay sees further failures after dedupe patch, ping me here and we'll attach logs to ENG-STREAM-1427. :thumbsup:
